title: How to organise the main workbench | Workshop
description:
The one surface where a project actually gets built, cut, glued, and repaired.

This is the Main Workbench in the Workshop. About 60-90 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
A bare bench top except the vise and the task lamp, one project tray holding the current job's parts, and a clear run of bench in front of the vise long enough to lay a board across. Every chisel and square back on its traced outline, the dog holes empty, and no offcuts or glue squeeze-out under the bench.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Clear the bench top and the shelf beneath it completely, then give every half-finished project a verdict: back
Straighten: Hang the tools your hand reaches for mid-cut, the marking knife, the combination square, the block plane, with
Shine: Vacuum the bench top and the dog holes rather than brushing them out, then scrape dried glue drips off the sur
Safety: Check the vise jaws still bite a test piece without slipping, and move the lamp cord so it does not lie across
Standardize: Trace the outlines on the tool wall in permanent marker so a gap reads as a missing chisel, then take one phot
Sustain: The last part of every session is the bench clear down, done before you take your safety glasses off, because

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
One project on the bench at a time, and the bench ends every session bare except the vise and the lamp.

Full written steps for this zone, free:
https://6s-success.com/zones/workshop-the-main-workbench.html

6S Success turns Lean's six-S method into something you can actually do in a house: Sort, Straighten, Shine, Safety, Standardize, Sustain. One small zone at a time, finished in one session, and it stays finished.
